candidate.title: ICE
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina ICE (inosine chemical erasing) row: RNA containing inosine is routed to untreated-control and acrylonitrile-treated branches, each with its own reverse-transcription/PCR block, yielding control cDNA versus the depicted failure across N1-cyanoethylinosine. This is a schematic of the ICE chemical discrimination principle, anchored to Sakurai et al. 2010 at abstract evidence level, with a secondary-catalogue NGS readout interface. The adjacent PSI-seq, Pseudo-seq and SHAPE-Seq rows are context. ICE-Seq papers and applications listed on the secondary page do not add target workflows or unshown library-preparation steps.

states.label: RNA containing an inosine residue
features: Biological target is inosine in RNA, interpreted in the sources as a marker of adenosine-to-inosine editing.
The input is drawn as T-C-I-C-G; the separate highlighted inosine-residue icon describes the target rather than an additional preparation step.
Letters are retained as schematic labels; no RNA strand orientation or chemical end groups are specified.

operations.label: Acrylonitrile
operations.description: Treat the lower-branch RNA with acrylonitrile, converting the depicted inosine residue into N1-cyanoethylinosine while retaining it in the RNA strand.
operations.mechanism: Cyanoethylation of inosine; acrylonitrile is the added chemical reagent, and the modified residue is explicitly labeled N1-cyanoethylinosine.
operations.information_effect: Changes the reverse-transcription behavior of the target residue; chemical erasing refers to loss of its representation in the downstream cDNA route, not physical excision of inosine.

operations.label: Reverse transcription / PCR amplification
operations.description: Apply the separately drawn reverse-transcription/PCR block to RNA bearing N1-cyanoethylinosine. The red X records failure to generate the corresponding amplifiable cDNA across the depicted modified residue; no material product for that example is drawn.

Differential cDNA representation supports detecting RNA inosine/A-to-I editing at this schematic level; the figure does not establish perfect specificity, quantitative editing fractions or a calling threshold.

checks.rationale: The candidate covers the assigned ICE chemical-discrimination schematic without adding adjacent assay rows or unshown library-preparation steps. All five material states, four local operations and eight material routes agree at their interfaces. The one-input/two-output operation records the control/treatment branch assignment; it does not merge independently processed samples. The two RT/PCR blocks remain distinct and lead to the correct cDNA versus X endpoints. RNA target, chemical substrate and DNA readout carrier are distinguished. Literal T-containing labels and the I-to-G sequence representation are identified as schematic labels without asserting a complementary-strand orientation or chemical end groups. The X is qualified to the illustrated modified template. The listed poster reference and all four supplied paper leads are assessed at their actual metadata/abstract evidence levels. The additional secondary-page 2014/2015 references are explicitly confined to bibliographic context. No consequential source conflict, unsupported chemistry, missing branch or architecture-changing unknown remains at this declared schematic scope.

evidence.quote: Here, we show that Myodonta clade-specific 4.5S RNAH (4.5SH), an abundant nuclear noncoding RNA that is highly homologous to the retrotransposon SINE B1, controls the expression of reporter gene that contains the antisense insertion of SINE B1 via nuclear retention.

evidence.locator: References, Ishida application summary
evidence.quote: They used cyanoethylation, as described in the ICE-Seq protocol, to observe nuclear retention upon depletion of endogenous 4.5SH.
